title: How to check coolant safely (engine cold only)
metaDesc: Check coolant only when the engine is cold. Never open a hot radiator or coolant cap. How to read the tank marks and add the right coolant.
first: Only check coolant when the engine is cold. Never open the radiator or coolant cap while the engine is hot: hot coolant can spray out and burn you.
Temperature gauge in the red, or steam from the hood? Pull over and turn the engine off. Don't open any cap until the engine is fully cold, which often takes 30 minutes or more.
Look at the see-through coolant tank. The level should be between the low and full marks.
If it's low, add the coolant type your manual lists, slowly, with the engine cold.
dont: Never open a hot radiator or coolant cap.
Don't put coolant in the windshield washer tank, or washer fluid in the coolant tank.
Don't keep driving if you have to keep adding coolant. That means a leak.

steps.t: Park and let the engine cool until the hood and engine are cool to the touch.
Look for a see-through plastic tank near the radiator. Your owner's manual shows where it is.
The tank has low and full marks (they may say MIN and MAX, or L and F). The coolant should be between them.
With the engine cold, open the tank cap slowly. Add the coolant your manual lists, a little at a time, up to the full mark. Close the cap tight.
Coolant shouldn't go down much. If you keep adding it, there's a leak. Get it checked.

call: If the temperature light comes on or the gauge goes into the red, pull over and turn the engine off. Have it checked before you drive again.
